true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Second `self.downsize` definition silently overrides the 5-argument one

Ruby has no method overloading, so the new `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 replaces the earlier `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145. The first definition is dead code. Any existing caller using the width/height form with an options hash (5 arguments) now raises `ArgumentError`. A caller passing 4 arguments binds `max_height` to `opts`, and `opts[:allow_animation]` then fails. Keep one signature and update all callers, or give the percentage form a different name.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client-side size limit hard-coded to 10MB for all upload types

`validateUploadedFile` used to read `max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb` from site settings, depending on `type`. It now uses a constant 10MB for both. The attachment limit is therefore ignored. If an admin sets it below 10MB, the client lets oversized files through and the server rejects them. If an admin sets it above 10MB, legitimate attachments are blocked on the client. The same hard-coded value is used in the 413 handler at line 246, so the error message no longer reports the real limit. Only images should get the 10MB cap, because the server now downsizes them. Attachments should keep using their setting.

true_positives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Downsizing uses the tempfile path, so the animated GIF branch is never taken and its arguments would be wrong

`optimize` chooses the animated (gifsicle) variant only when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. Rack and Tempfile paths have no extension, so an uploaded GIF never takes that branch. The static `convert from[0] -resize 80%>` path runs instead and flattens an animated GIF to its first frame, even with `allow_animation` enabled. If the branch were taken, `resize_instructions_animated` would emit `--resize-fit 80%`, which gifsicle does not accept (it takes `WxH`, or `--scale`). The in-place conversion also writes to an extensionless output path, so the output format is inferred and is not guaranteed for formats such as SVG. The code should work from the real filename or extension and handle GIFs explicitly.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

false_positives.candidate:
Hard-coded 10MB download cap and no server-side bound before running ImageMagick up to 5 times

The API URL download limit changed from the configured `max_image_size_kb` to a literal `10.megabytes`. This is also used for non-image attachments. The only enforcement of the 10MB limit for direct uploads is the client JS, which is trivially bypassed. The server now runs `convert` up to 5 times, synchronously inside `Scheduler::Defer`, on whatever size and dimensions arrive. A user can upload a very large or decompression-bomb image and consume CPU and memory repeatedly. Enforce a server-side maximum input size (and ideally dimensions) before downsizing.

No tests for the new auto-downsize behaviour or the changed OptimizedImage API

The PR adds an auto-downsize loop in the uploads controller. It also changes the signatures of `OptimizedImage.resize`, `downsize` and `optimize` and removes `dimensions`. No tests were added or updated for any of it. The duplicate `downsize` definition would have been caught by a basic spec. Add specs for uploading an oversized image, for the setting set to 0, and for the `OptimizedImage` methods.

Return value of `downsize` ignored; failures retried 5 times and oversized file still used

`OptimizedImage.downsize` returns false when `convert` fails, for example when the file is corrupt or the format is unsupported. The loop ignores that result and runs the same failing command up to 5 times. It then falls through to `Upload.create_for` with the original file. Break out of the loop when `downsize` returns false. Also note that five passes of 80% only shrink each dimension to about 33%, which may not be enough for very large files. Such files then fail with a generic size error.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Missing params cause 500s; nil host blows up in the model's before_validation

`params[:embeddable_host][:host]` raises if the `embeddable_host` key is absent. If `host` is absent or nil, `EmbeddableHost`'s `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!` on nil and raises NoMethodError. Both cases give a 500 instead of a validation error from `render_json_error`. The model callback should guard against nil, and the controller should use `params.require(:embeddable_host)`. The category id is also never checked to exist.

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
update/destroy dereference nil when the host id doesn't exist

`EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for an unknown or already-deleted id. `save_host(nil)` then calls `host.host=` on nil, and `destroy` calls `host.destroy` on nil. Both raise NoMethodError, so the client gets a 500 instead of a 404. Double-clicking delete or editing a stale list would trigger this. Use `find_by` plus an explicit not-found response, or `find`, so `RecordNotFound` is handled.

true_positives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Host lookup ignores case of the input and can never match hosts stored with a port

The query is `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`, where `host` is `uri.host` taken straight from the referer or embed URL. Only the column is lowercased, so a referer such as `http://Example.COM/...` never matches a stored `example.com`. The validation regex explicitly allows a `:port` suffix, and `before_validation` only strips from the first `/`, so `example.com:8080` is stored with its port. `uri.host` never includes a port, so such a record can never match any request. Normalize with `host.downcase` and decide consistently whether ports are stored or compared.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migrated hosts are inserted raw: not normalized, not SQL-escaped, blanks not skipped

The old `embeddable_hosts` setting allowed entries like `http://eviltrout.com` and values with surrounding whitespace or blank lines. The migration inserts each line verbatim with string interpolation, so it bypasses the model's `before_validation` that strips the scheme and path. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` with `URI(...).host`, so a row stored as `http://eviltrout.com` can never match. Every site that used the documented scheme-prefixed format silently loses embedding after upgrade. Blank lines become empty-host rows, and a quote in a value breaks the SQL statement. Strip the scheme and path, strip whitespace, skip blanks, and quote with `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Fabricator file contents are swapped between category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb

`category_fabricator.rb` now holds only `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`. The `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category` fabricators were moved into `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. Fabrication loads every file in the directory, so tests still run. But the file names no longer match their contents, so anyone looking for the category fabricators will not find them. It also looks like a copy/rename mistake that will cause confusion or merge conflicts later. Each file should contain its own fabricators.

true_positives.golden_comment: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migrated hosts are inserted raw: not normalized, not SQL-escaped, blanks not skipped

The old `embeddable_hosts` setting allowed entries like `http://eviltrout.com` and values with surrounding whitespace or blank lines. The migration inserts each line verbatim with string interpolation, so it bypasses the model's `before_validation` that strips the scheme and path. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` with `URI(...).host`, so a row stored as `http://eviltrout.com` can never match. Every site that used the documented scheme-prefixed format silently loses embedding after upgrade. Blank lines become empty-host rows, and a quote in a value breaks the SQL statement. Strip the scheme and path, strip whitespace, skip blanks, and quote with `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration crashes with NoMethodError when `embed_category` (or `uncategorized_category_id`) has no row in site_settings

`execute("SELECT ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` indexes into a PG::Result. Sites that never changed `embed_category` have no row in `site_settings`, because defaults are not stored. Fresh installs and most upgraded sites are in this case. `[0]` is then nil and `nil['id']` raises, so the whole migration aborts and `embeddable_hosts` is never created. The fallback on line 15 has the same problem: `execute("SELECT value ... 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value']` fails if that row is missing. Use `.first`/`.ntuples` checks and fall back to a default instead of assuming a row exists.

false_positives.candidate:
Client assigns a category that may differ from what the server saved

When no category is chosen, the server falls back to the uncategorized category id. After saving, the component sets `host.category` to `Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))`, which is undefined for a blank id. The row then shows an empty category badge until the page is reloaded, even though the server stored Uncategorized. Use the `category_id` from the server response instead of the local `categoryId`.

Host validation is overly restrictive and there is no uniqueness check

The regex requires a final label of 2-5 letters. This rejects `localhost`, intranet names, IPs and longer TLDs such as `.photography` or `.technology`. The old free-text setting accepted these, so admins can no longer add or re-save them. There is also no uniqueness validation on `host`, so the same host can be added repeatedly, each with a possibly different category. Which category an imported topic gets is then arbitrary, because `.first` has no ordering.

New admin endpoints have no behavioral tests

The new `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` and `Admin::EmbeddingController` are covered only by a test that they subclass AdminController. There are no tests for create/update/destroy, validation errors, a missing id, default-category fallback, or non-staff access. The 500 paths in the controller therefore go unnoticed. The migration is also untested.

expandable_first_post? specs have a misleading name and a no-op fixture

`expandable_first_post?` no longer looks at embeddable hosts. The test "is false if embeddable_host is blank" actually passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and there is no topic embed, so it does not test what its name says. In the `'with an emeddable host'` context (typo included) the `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` has no effect on the result. The specs should be renamed or cleaned up to reflect the new behavior.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`TopicUser.find_by` can return nil, causing a 500 in `unsubscribe`

`tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` returns nil when the logged-in user has no `topic_users` row for that topic, which is the case for any other user who opens the URL. The next line, `tu.notification_level`, then raises NoMethodError and the user gets a 500 error page. The action should create the row, for example via `TopicUser.change`, or handle the nil case.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
Explicit `render :show` makes `show` render before `canonical_url` is set

`perform_show_response` now calls `render :show` inside the `format.html` block. In `show`, `perform_show_response` is called first and `canonical_url UrlHelper.absolute_without_cdn(...)` is called right after it. Previously the template rendered implicitly after the action returned, so the canonical URL was set before the layout ran. Now the view and layout are rendered immediately inside `perform_show_response`, so the later `canonical_url` call has no effect on the HTML. Topic pages will lose the correct `<link rel="canonical">` and fall back to the request URL, for example `/t/slug/id/5`. That is an SEO regression on every topic page. Fix by calling `canonical_url` before `perform_show_response`, or by rendering only in `unsubscribe`.

No tests for the new unsubscribe action, URL helper, or email content

The only spec change adds an `unsubscribe_url` option to an existing message-builder example. There is no controller spec for `TopicsController#unsubscribe`: login required, slug redirect, level transitions, missing `TopicUser` row, JSON vs HTML. There is no spec for `Topic#unsubscribe_url`. There is no spec that the notification email actually contains the per-topic unsubscribe link in both the HTML and text parts. The nil-`TopicUser` crash and the idempotency problem above would have been caught by such tests.

Notification level changed with `save!` instead of `TopicUser.change`

The action sets `tu.notification_level` directly and calls `tu.save!`. This bypasses `TopicUser.change`, which also sets `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` (user_changed) and publishes the `notification_level_change` MessageBus message. With `notifications_reason_id` left unchanged (often NULL), `TopicUser.update_last_read` will later auto-promote the topic back to `tracking` once the user has read enough. That silently undoes the mute or unsubscribe. Open clients also never receive the level change. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`.

State-changing, non-idempotent toggle behind a GET route `unsubscribe` is routed as a GET and mutates the user's notification level on every request. Each reload or repeat visit steps it down further: watching/tracking becomes regular, regular becomes muted, muted stays muted. A single click followed by a refresh, or the back button, therefore mutes the topic instead of just unsubscribing. Because it is a GET with no CSRF protection, any third-party page that embeds `` can mute topics for a logged-in visitor. The `.json` format variant mutates as well. The action should compute a deterministic target state, or require an explicit POST/PUT from the confirmation page.

`unsubscribe_link` string now requires `%{unsubscribe_url}`, which breaks callers that omit it

The English `unsubscribe_link` string now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Both `html_part` (line 67) and `body` (line 90) call `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)`. Any caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also passing `unsubscribe_url` (other mailers, plugins, existing specs) now raises `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` when the email is built. The spec had to be edited to pass `unsubscribe_url` for exactly this reason. The builder should supply a fallback or only include the per-topic sentence when `unsubscribe_url` is present.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Validation has a DB-write side effect, so match_count is over-counted

`should_block?` increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at` and saves the record. It is called from `EmailValidator#validate_each`, which runs on every validation of a user whose email changed. `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save`, which validates again. A single signup attempt with a blocked email therefore bumps the counter twice. Any other `valid?` call on a new or changed user does the same. Statistics collection and validation should be separate. Record the hit only when the block actually rejects a save, or do it explicitly in the controller.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive, so it can be bypassed

`BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` is an exact, case-sensitive match. Email addresses are case-insensitive, and the rest of the app normalizes with `Email.downcase`. A blocked address like `bad@spammers.org` can be bypassed by registering `Bad@Spammers.org`. The `uniqueness: true` validation and the unique index on `blocked_emails.email` are also case-sensitive, so case-variant duplicates can be stored. Normalize to lowercase on save and on lookup, or compare with `lower(email)`.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

false_positives.candidate:
Block check is skipped whenever any earlier error exists on the attribute

The blocked-email check only runs if `record.errors[attribute].blank?`. Presence and uniqueness validators run first, so a duplicate email never reaches the check. Hit statistics for a blocked address are skipped whenever another error is present. The condition also depends on validator declaration order, which is fragile. Make the block check independent of other errors, or document that it is intentionally conditional.

Every server-side email error is shown as a generic 'invalid' email

On any failed signup where `result.errors.email` is present, the submitted email is added to `rejectedEmails`. `emailValidation` then shows `user.email.invalid` for that address. The server error may be that the email is already taken, is not allowed from that provider, or is blocked. All of these now show the same generic message, which can mislead the user. The list is also never cleared and is declared as `Em.A([])` on the controller prototype, so it is shared state.

Moved whitelist/blacklist logic and the double-validation side effect are not tested

The whitelist/blacklist domain logic moved from `User#email_validator` into `EmailValidator`, but the new validator spec only covers the blocked-email stub. No test covers the whitelist or blacklist branches, or the skip-when-already-errored behavior. Nothing checks that a signup with a blocked email returns the new `errors`/`values` fields from `UsersController#create`. Nothing covers case variants of a blocked address, and no test exposes that validating twice increments `match_count` twice.

Read-modify-write counter update loses concurrent increments

`record.match_count += 1; record.save` is a read-modify-write on an in-memory copy. Two concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked address can both read N and both write N+1, losing a count. `save` also runs the model validations, including the uniqueness query, on every hit. An atomic update such as `BlockedEmail.increment_counter` or `update_all("match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?")` avoids both problems.

true_positives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Kernel#open on an admin-supplied string allows command execution and local file reads

`SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses `Kernel#open` (open-uri patched) on a site-setting string. If the value starts with `|`, `open` runs it as a shell command. A plain path reads local files. Site admins are not normally trusted with shell access on the server. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` and `disqus.thor` use the same pattern. Parse the URL, require an http(s) scheme, and call `URI.parse(url).open`, with explicit timeouts.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Substring check on message origin is not a valid origin validation

`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of `discourseUrl`. For `http://forum.example.com/`, a message from `http://forum.example.co` passes. The check also ignores `e.source`, and `e.data.height` is applied unvalidated. Compare `e.origin` for exact equality against the origin of `discourseUrl`, check `e.source === iframe.contentWindow`, and coerce height to a bounded number.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate: URL interpolated unescaped into the HTML footer, and URL check uses multiline `^` `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` uses `^`, which matches at the start of any line, so a value like `"junk\nhttp://x"` passes. The URL is then interpolated unescaped into `#{url}`, and the result is stored with the raw_html cook method, which does no sanitizing. A feed item `` or `` containing `'` or `<` can therefore break out of the attribute and inject markup. Validate with `\A...\z` or `URI.parse`, and HTML-escape the URL (`ERB::Util.h`) before building the footer.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`<%- end if %>` is malformed ERB/Ruby

`end if` ends the block and then applies a dangling `if` modifier to whatever expression the ERB compiler emits next (the following output-buffer append). It only works by accident and obscures the template's logic. It should be `<%- end %>`. Separately, the logo links in the header (line 8) and footer (line 26) lack `target: '_blank'`, so clicking the logo loads the entire forum inside the small embed iframe.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feed items without `content` crash the whole poll

`i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when an item has no `content`. Many RSS 2.0 feeds provide only `<description>`, so `i.content` is nil. One such item aborts the loop, and every later item in the feed is skipped on every run. `String#scrub` also requires Ruby 2.1+, which may not match the supported Ruby versions. Fall back to `description`, skip items with blank content, and rescue per item so one bad entry does not stop the import.

true_positives.golden_comment: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Referer emitted into a JS string with HTML escaping

`'<%= request.referer %>'` uses HTML escaping inside a `<script>` block. `&` becomes `&` and `'` becomes `'`, and a backslash is not escaped. The value is only coincidentally harmless, because the host was validated and postMessage uses only the origin part. A referer ending in `\` breaks the string literal and the resize message. Use `<%= raw request.referer.to_json %>`, or better the validated `embeddable_host` origin, rather than the raw Referer.

false_negatives.golden_comment: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

false_positives.candidate:
Disqus importer loses `--category` and now requires live HTTP fetches

The `-c/--category` option was removed, so existing invocations now fail and imported topics can no longer be placed in a category. The topic's `created_at` from Disqus is also dropped, so topics get the import time. Each thread now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote` on the thread link, which makes a network fetch. A 404 or timeout raises and aborts the whole import. A non-http link makes `import` return nil, so the thread is silently skipped. This changes the tool's behavior without fallback or documentation.

Embed import paths are barely tested

The specs only cover a malformed URL, the happy create path, and a trivial update. Nothing covers `import_remote`, `PollFeed#poll_feed` (nil content, relative links), the unchanged-hash path, the deleted-post path, or the HTML-escaping of the footer URL. Those are exactly where the bugs above live.

Existing embed whose post was deleted causes NoMethodError on every re-import

In the update branch, `post = embed.post` is nil if the post was trashed, because Trashable scopes out deleted posts. When the content hash changes, `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises. In PollFeed that aborts the rest of the feed every hour. The stale `topic_embeds` row also prevents the URL from ever being re-imported. Handle a missing post: skip, or remove the embed and re-create.

Negative-condition specs pass vacuously

"requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" stub only one setting and leave `feed_polling_enabled?` at its default of false. `poll_feed` is therefore never called, whatever those conditions do. Each test should enable the other settings so it actually exercises the condition it names. Similarly, `embed_controller_spec`'s "is 404 without an embed_url" fails earlier at `ensure_embeddable` (no referer), not on the missing parameter, so it does not test what it claims.

Only the Rails 4 lockfile is updated for the new gems

The new `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` gems are added to the shared Gemfile and `Gemfile_rails4.lock`. The Rails 3 lock (`Gemfile.lock`, used when `RAILS3` is set, as this Gemfile supports) is not updated. That boot mode will fail under frozen/deployment bundling, or silently re-resolve versions.

Protocol-relative URLs are mangled by absolutize_urls

Any `href`/`src` beginning with `/` is rewritten as `prefix + '/' + href.sub(/^\/+/, '')`. A protocol-relative URL such as `//cdn.example.com/a.jpg` becomes `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/a.jpg`, which is a broken link or image. Skip values starting with `//`, or resolve with `URI.join(url, href)`, which also handles `../x` and `images/x.png`.

Unauthenticated requests can trigger unbounded fetches and topic creation

The only gate is the spoofable Referer header plus a per-URL 60s throttle. Any client can request `/embed/best?embed_url=` with arbitrarily many distinct URLs on the embeddable host (for example, differing query strings). Each distinct URL enqueues a job, and each job polls the entire feed synchronously (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute`) and fetches the page. If it parses, the page is turned into a new topic, so URLs with different query strings each get their own. This allows unlimited topic creation and outbound-request amplification. Add a global rate limit, URL normalization, and possibly an allowed-path/pattern setting.

Unrelated edit to an existing migration adds `force: true`, which drops the table

This PR modifies an already-committed migration to add `force: true` to `create_table :top_topics`. `force: true` drops any existing `top_topics` table before creating it, so re-running or resetting this migration destroys data. The change has nothing to do with embedding. The same file set also includes a whitespace-only edit to `20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` (and it removes the trailing newline). Revert both edits to old migrations, and avoid `force: true` unless it is truly intended.

Wrapping PostCreator in an outer transaction enqueues jobs before commit

`PostCreator#create` deliberately enqueues `process_post` and `feature_topic_users` after its own transaction, so workers cannot see uncommitted rows (see the comment in `enqueue_jobs`). Wrapping it in `Topic.transaction` here defeats that: the jobs and the TopicTrackingState/MessageBus publishes fire before the outer transaction commits. If `TopicEmbed.create!` then fails, for example on the unique `embed_url` index when PollFeed and RetrieveTopic race, the transaction rolls back but the jobs and notifications for the non-existent post have already gone out. Create the embed row outside this wrapping transaction, or handle the failure explicitly.

`open(url)` used without requiring open-uri

`import_remote` calls `open(url).read` but this file never requires `open-uri`. It only works if `jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` (which has the require) or some gem happened to load it first. Otherwise `Kernel#open` treats the URL as a filename and raises Errno::ENOENT. This is likely in the thor Disqus import and in a lazily-loaded dev/test environment. Add `require 'open-uri'` here and prefer `URI.parse(url).open`.

`post.present?` is always true for an unsaved post, so create! can fail on null post_id

`PostCreator#create` returns `@post` even when saving failed and it rolled back, in which case the post is unsaved with `errors` populated. An ActiveRecord object is always `present?`, so the code goes on to `TopicEmbed.create!(post_id: post.id ...)` with nil ids. That raises a DB NOT NULL violation (`post_id` is `null: false`) instead of failing cleanly. Check `post.persisted?` or `creator.errors.blank?`.

raw_html cook method skips all sanitization, so imported feed HTML is stored and served as-is (stored XSS)

`Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == :raw_html`, bypassing the cooking pipeline and its sanitizer. `TopicEmbed.import` feeds this path with unsanitized RSS/Atom item content (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)` in PollFeed) and with remote page HTML. That content is stored in `posts.cooked` and rendered unescaped with `raw post.cooked` in `embed/best.html.erb` and in the main forum UI. Any `<script>`, `onerror=` or `javascript:` payload in a third-party feed, or injected into a compromised feed, therefore runs in the forum's origin. The cook step also runs on every later save, so editing does not clean it. Sanitize the HTML (for example with the already-bundled `sanitize` gem and a whitelist) before storing or rendering it.

setnx followed by expire is not atomic

If the process dies or Redis errors between `setnx` and `expire`, the `retrieved:<url>` key stays forever and that URL can never be retrieved again by non-staff users. Use a single atomic `SET key value NX EX 60` call (or `setex` semantics) instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
align-items mixin passes modern values to legacy box-align properties and emits a nonexistent property

The mixin writes `$alignment` unchanged into `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`. Those legacy properties use different keywords (`start`/`end` instead of `flex-start`/`flex-end`). `center` and `baseline`, the only values used today, happen to be valid in both. Any future call such as `align-items(flex-start)` will produce invalid legacy declarations, and old browsers will silently ignore them. `-ms-align-items` (line 121) does not exist in any IE/Edge implementation and is dead output. The mixin looks safe for all inputs when it is not.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

false_positives.candidate:
Custom-message paragraph spacing removed

`.small-action-desc .custom-message p` changed from `margin: 5px 0` to `margin: 0`. Custom messages are rendered as cooked HTML and can contain several paragraphs. They now run together with no vertical separation. The spacing was not needed to fix the flex centering, so this is an unrelated visual regression.

Float declarations inside the new flex container have no effect, so the button no longer right-aligns

`.small-action` is now `display: flex`, but `.topic-avatar { float: left }` and `button { float: right }` are left in place. Floats are ignored on flex items. If the button is a flex item of `.small-action`, the intended right alignment is lost and it sits right after the description text. `.small-action-desc` has no `flex: 1` or auto margin to absorb the free space. The stale float rules are misleading, and the button positioning should be reworked explicitly, for example with `margin-left: auto`.

Panel right-alignment now depends on `margin-left: auto`, which legacy flexbox fallbacks don't support

The panel used to be pushed right with `float: right`. That was replaced by `margin-left: auto` on a flex item. The new mixins emit legacy `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` fallbacks. In those 2009-era flexbox implementations, auto margins do not absorb free space the way they do in the modern spec. A browser that takes the legacy path will therefore render the user/search panel directly after the title instead of at the right edge. Floats are also ignored on flex items, so there is no fallback. Either drop the legacy-prefix claim or add a legacy-compatible alignment such as `-webkit-box-flex: 1` on the spacer or title.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
include_website_name is missing the trailing '?' so it is never called

ActiveModel::Serializers only consults `include_<attr>?` methods. The method is defined as `include_website_name` without the `?`, so it is dead code and the attribute is always emitted. When there is no website, `website_name` is serialized as `null` instead of being omitted. The guard also would not have covered the restricted-user case, because it checks `website.present?` and not `scope.restrict_user_fields?`. Rename it to `include_website_name?`, or drop it and use `untrusted_attributes` instead.

false_positives.candidate:
Fragile host-matching logic; `"." << website_host` mutates a string literal

`"" << website_host` appends to a string literal. This works only while string literals are not frozen; with `frozen_string_literal` or a newer Ruby it raises `FrozenError` and breaks serialization of every user with a website. Use `".#{website_host}"` instead. The same-label-count branch compares everything after the first label. That treats unrelated sites on a shared public suffix as siblings, for example `foo.co.uk` and `forum.co.uk`, and shows the full path. The code also parses the URI up to three times per call; parse it once into a local.

Missing tests for the sibling-subdomain branch, blank website, and untrusted users

The new tests cover only three of the branches in `website_name`: a different domain, an identical domain, and a parent domain. They do not test the `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` branch (same label count, shared parent), a blank or unparseable website, or the TL0-anonymous case. The `untrusted_attributes` list at line 11 omits `website_name`, so the information leak described above is not caught. Add cases for these paths.

website_name is not in untrusted_attributes, so it leaks the hidden website for TL0 users

`website` is in the `untrusted_attributes` list, so it is omitted for TL0 users when the viewer is anonymous (`scope.restrict_user_fields?`). The new `website_name` attribute is not in that list. It is still serialized, and it carries the host and sometimes the path of the very website that was meant to be hidden. The template now renders `model.website_name` instead of the old controller property derived from `model.website`. Before this change a hidden website produced no name at all, so this is a regression in the spam-protection behaviour. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` and to the matching list in the spec.

website_name is now a static server value and goes stale after the user edits their website

The old `websiteName` was a client computed property depending on `model.website`, so it updated as soon as the website changed. `website_name` is now a plain attribute that is only set by `findDetails`. `User.save` sends `website` but only copies `bio_excerpt` back from the response. After a user changes their website in preferences and returns to their profile, the same user model is reused. The profile then shows the old `website_name` until a full reload, while the link `href` already uses the new `website`. Refresh `website_name` from the save response, or keep deriving it client-side.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

false_positives.candidate:
Admin group API contract changed silently: params no longer nested under `group`, usernames and PATCH changes dropped

`create` and `update` now read flat `params[:name]` / `params[:visible]` instead of `params[:group][...]`. `usernames` and the PATCH `changes[add/delete]` incremental API are gone, replaced by new `/members` endpoints. External scripts or plugins using the old shape get no error. `update` sends `visible` as absent, so it resets visibility to false, and name changes are ignored. `create` sees an empty name and fails validation. This is a breaking API change that is not documented in the PR description ("Test 8").

Public group members page now shows only the first 50 members with no way to page

The public members route calls `model.findMembers()` and renders `members`. The server now caps results at the default limit of 50, and this template and its route have no next/previous controls. Non-automatic groups used to return every member, so any group with more than 50 members now silently shows a truncated list to users with no way to see the rest. Pagination was only added to the admin UI. The `{{#if model}}` guard is also always truthy now that the model is the group itself.

Response shape of /groups/:name/members changed from array to {members, meta} and default is now capped at 50, with no spec coverage

`members` used to return a bare array (all members for non-automatic groups, 200 for automatic ones). It now returns `{members:, meta:}` and defaults to 50 rows. Any other client, plugin or existing spec that parses the array breaks, and nothing in the PR adds or updates a spec for the new payload, the `meta` values, or limit/offset behaviour (groups_controller_spec is untouched).

limit/offset are taken from params without validation or an upper bound

`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are passed straight to the query. A negative limit or offset makes PostgreSQL raise and returns a 500. `limit=0` returns nothing, and the admin UI then computes `user_count / 0` (Infinity). A very large limit lets any caller who can see the group pull the whole member list in one request, so the pagination does not bound anything. Clamp limit to a sane range (e.g. 1..max) and offset to >= 0.

remove_member uses group.users.delete(id) instead of Group#remove, bypassing callbacks and failing for non-members

The old incremental-delete code called `group.remove(user)`. The new code calls `group.users.delete(user_id)` with a raw integer. On a has_many :through association this deletes the join rows without running GroupUser destroy callbacks, so any cleanup tied to the join model (e.g. primary group or title) is skipped. When given an id, Rails also does a `find` on the association, so a user who is not in the group (stale UI, double click) raises RecordNotFound and returns an error instead of succeeding silently, as the old PATCH delete did.

usernames input is never cleared or reset, so it leaks across groups and repeats on re-add

`usernames` is a property on the singleton admin-group controller. It is not cleared after `addMembers` (acknowledged by the TODO) and not reset when the route sets up a different group. Usernames typed or left over for group A are still in the selector when the admin opens group B, and pressing Add adds them to B. `addMembers` and `removeMember` also have no failure handler, so a rejected request gives the admin no feedback.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

false_positives.candidate:
Fallback locales are only loaded by the controller filter, not by translate itself

`I18n.translate` still lazy-loads only `config.locale`. The new fallback chain is `[locale, site default, :en]`, and `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is called only from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Any code outside a web request does not go through that filter. This includes Sidekiq jobs, mailers using `I18n.with_locale`, rake tasks and the console. In those contexts a key missing from the current locale falls back to locales that were never loaded, unless some earlier request in the same process happened to load them. For example, when the site default is `fr`, English is never loaded in a job process. The result is a "translation missing: ..." string instead of the English fallback. The loading should happen inside `translate`/`load_locale` for every locale in the chain, not in one controller filter.

Fallback lookup reads SiteSetting and allocates an array on every translate call

`I18n::Backend::Fallbacks#translate` calls `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` on every lookup, not only when a key is missing. Each call now evaluates `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` and builds a new array through `uniq` and `compact`. Calls with arguments bypass the LRU cache in `translate_accelerator`, so they pay this cost every time. It also ties every translation to SiteSetting being readable. If `default_locale` were nil or unavailable, `nil.to_sym` would raise from inside I18n. The chain could be memoized per `(locale, default_locale)` instead.

Fallbacks now enabled in every environment with no tests

The PR removes `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` from the production, profile and cloud66 configs. It installs a custom `FallbackLocaleList` unconditionally, so dev and test now have fallbacks too, where they previously did not. No spec covers the new behavior: chain ordering (user, site default, en), lazy loading of the fallback locales, or the 'translation missing' case. Specs that relied on missing-translation behavior in a non-English locale may also silently change. A spec for `FallbackLocaleList#[]`, `ensure_loaded!` and an end-to-end lookup of a key present only in `en` should be added.

LRU cache key ignores the fallback chain, so cached results go stale

The cache key is `key + config.locale + backend.object_id`. The result now also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale`, which `FallbackLocaleList` puts in the chain. If a key is missing in the current locale, the value served from the site default locale (or the 'translation missing' string) is cached under the current locale only. After an admin changes `default_locale`, or after a fallback locale is loaded later, the process keeps returning the old cached fallback until the cache is evicted or `reload!` runs. The key should include the fallback chain or the default locale, or the cache should be cleared when `default_locale` changes.

Call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments does not compile

Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, so passkeys are never set up on the initial login

The new helper returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. It is used in `authenticate()` and in `challenge(context, error, field)`. On a normal first login `context.getUser()` is null, so the helper returns false and `fillContextForm` is never called. The old code did call it when the user was null. The login page then has no conditional-UI/passkey form, and the "username webauthn" autocomplete and `//form[@id='webauth']` checks in the existing tests fail. The same happens on the error path after an invalid username, because the user is still null there. The condition should be `user == null || <user has a passkey credential>`. false_positives.candidate:
Override of shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators is missing @Override

`shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` overrides the new protected method in `WebAuthnAuthenticator` but has no `@Override` annotation. A later signature change in the parent would silently turn it into an unrelated method, and conditional-UI would again show or require the allowed authenticators list.

Passkey UI is enabled for any pre-set user without checking whether the user has a passkey credential

For the re-authentication case the helper only checks that realm passkeys are enabled and that a user is present. It never checks that the user has a passwordless/WebAuthn credential. A user with no passkey is therefore shown the conditional-UI passkey form during re-authentication. reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey disables passkeys for the realm, so it does not cover its stated scenario

The test is meant to show that a user without a passkey does not see passkeys during re-authentication. It sets `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)` for the whole realm, so nothing passkey-related would be shown for anyone. The real case, passkeys enabled in the realm but the user has no passkey credential, is untested. That case is the one the missing credential check in `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` would break. The try/`fail()`/`catch (Exception)` pattern also hides the intent. Use `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` or check for absence directly.

true_positives.golden_comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Negative-offset slicing is unsupported by the Django ORM and the comment claiming otherwise is wrong

When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code runs `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django querysets do not support negative indexing and raise (`ValueError`/`AssertionError`: "Negative indexing is not supported"). The comment "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is false. A client who supplies a cursor such as `0:-5:1` (`Cursor.from_string` accepts negative offsets) triggers an unhandled exception and a 500. `stop = start_offset + limit + extra` can also go negative. The branch cannot deliver the advertised "access to data beyond normal pagination bounds", and it adds a user-controlled error path to an admin endpoint. If negative offsets are meant to be supported, they need real handling, or an explicit `BadPaginationError`.

true_positives.golden_comment: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`organization_context.member` may be None and the check is evaluated on every request

`enable_advanced` is computed eagerly, before checking `use_optimized`. For a non-superuser, `organization_context.member` can be `None` (for example, non-member or token-based access), so `.has_global_access` raises `AttributeError`. This would break the default audit-log listing for requests that never asked for optimized pagination. Compute the flag only when `use_optimized` is true, and guard against `member is None`.

true_positives.golden_comment: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
OptimizedCursorPaginator uses numeric key handling for a datetime sort key, so the optimized path crashes

The endpoint passes `order_by="-datetime"` to `OptimizedCursorPaginator`. Its `get_item_key` copies `Paginator.get_item_key` (`math.floor(getattr(item, self.key))`), not `DateTimePaginator`'s. For `AuditLogEntry.datetime` this calls `math.floor` on a `datetime` and raises `TypeError` as soon as `build_cursor` computes the key for the first result. `value_from_cursor` (lines 842-843) also returns the raw integer cursor value instead of converting milliseconds to a timezone-aware datetime, so `build_queryset` would compare the datetime column to an integer on any follow-up page. Every `?optimized_pagination=true` request that returns rows fails with a 500, or with a SQL error on later pages.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Importing non-existent OptimizedCursorPaginator

false_positives.candidate:
Change to shared BasePaginator silently alters behavior for every paginator and contradicts its own comment

The edit to `BasePaginator.get_result`, which every `Paginator`/`DateTimePaginator` consumer in Sentry uses, claims to "allow negative offsets". In reality `max(0, offset)` clamps negative offsets to 0 for forward cursors, so a malformed or tampered cursor now silently returns the first page instead of failing. For `is_prev` cursors the negative offset is still passed straight to the queryset and raises. The behavior is inconsistent, changes a global code path for an unrelated feature, and the "safe because the queryset handles boundary conditions" comment is incorrect. This hunk should be reverted or replaced with explicit validation (`BadPaginationError` for offset < 0).

Comment claims Cursor allows negative offsets, but nothing supports them downstream

The added comment says negative offsets are allowed for advanced pagination and enable efficient reverse pagination. `Cursor` already accepted negative ints, and no logic was added. The downstream consumers (Django slicing) reject negative indices, so the comment is misleading documentation of a non-working feature.

New query parameter, paginator and endpoint branch have no tests

The PR adds an undocumented `optimized_pagination` query parameter, a new paginator class and a privileged code path with no tests. No test exercises the optimized path, the authorization gate (superuser / global access vs. regular admin), or negative-offset cursors. A basic test of the optimized path would have caught the `math.floor(datetime)` crash, so the new behavior is currently unverified.

OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result and delivers no actual optimization

The class copies about 60 lines of `BasePaginator.get_result`, differing only in the negative-offset branch. Both branches build the same queryset and the same slice, so the "optimized query path" and "streamlined boundary condition handling" in the docstring do not exist. It also copies `Paginator.get_item_key`/`value_from_cursor` rather than subclassing the correct `DateTimePaginator`, which is how the datetime bug above arose. Any future fix to `BasePaginator.get_result` will have to be mirrored here by hand. The docstring and PR title are misleading, since there is no performance change.

Trailing whitespace and stray blank lines will fail lint

Lines 72 and 89 in the endpoint have trailing whitespace. The paginator docstring also has trailing-whitespace lines and three consecutive blank lines before `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, and a stray trailing blank line at the end of the file. These will trip the repo's pre-commit/flake8/black checks.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Negative-offset slice on a Django QuerySet raises instead of paginating; justifying comments are wrong

When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code runs `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise `AssertionError("Negative indexing is not supported.")`. A user-supplied cursor such as `0:-5:0` (`Cursor.from_string` accepts negative offsets) therefore produces a 500. The comments are wrong on two counts. "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing" is false. "This is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level" does not apply, because the slice does not become a valid read of earlier rows. This feature is exposed to superusers and global-access members, so it is a crash path in new code, not an optimization.

true_positives.golden_comment: In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
